changes.scan_shows: The horizontal cancellation crosses the final letter group. A trailing lower hook can belong to the plural s, but the ending cannot be fully isolated from the crossing stroke. Retained C doubt.
An upper word has initial c, tall h, p descender and final s; the intervening a/m strokes are faint enough to retain C’s uncertainty. Its position above the cancelled noun establishes replacement.

At the position after the i and before the g, only a short horizontal stroke is secure; its possible n shoulder is faded. The g descender and following l/é/s traces survive. Added the explicit dash alternative instead of completing the n from the spelling.
The small left loop hangs from a long horizontal top stroke extending right; this is not a closed o body. C doubt resolved.

changes.place: Cancelled letter immediately before L tensor L
changes.scan_shows: A left upright and oblique right arms suggest K, but several cancelling strokes cross the area and leave L possible. The following live L is separate and clear. Partial glyph alternatives are recoverable, so no illegible-word token is used for this mathematical letter.
The apparent high ink belongs to the connected head of a; the enlarged crop shows no separate grave accent above it. C doubt resolved.
Paired high short strokes appear at both ends, not angled guillemets. Settled in half_a. Approximate WHOLE-source box [540, 850, 827, 925]; no reader crop was made for this already settled locus.
An open loop crosses into a right tail, followed by a separate bowed low comma. There is no opening parenthesis and no radiating star.

A compact crossed group follows the two colon points. A low u-like bowl remains, while the right continuation is obscured and does not securely distinguish u from un. H neither transcribes nor describes this cancellation.
Two adjacent t uprights and one following looped e are present; there are no o/u letters between them. This was settled in half_b, and is also visible as context in c07.

changes.place: Verb after sur un objet quelconque de X

Approximate WHOLE-source box [300, 1245, 615, 1320]; no reader crop was made for this settled locus.

Both quotation ends consist of paired raised strokes, followed at the right by the separate sentence stop. Settled in half_b. Approximate WHOLE-source box [120, 1385, 510, 1460]; no reader crop was made for this settled locus.
Paired high pen strokes surround the word; no angled guillemets. Settled in half_b. Approximate WHOLE-source box [115, 1530, 355, 1620]; no reader crop was made for this settled locus.

The H has a lower-left loop, an upper-right loop and a transverse joining stroke. It is a cursive/script form rather than doubled parallel uprights. The caligraphic/script font alternatives are retained because neither printed form reproduces the pen exactly.

changes.place: Mark after E in final formula
changes.scan_shows: A single short detached oblique stroke stands at the upper right of E, without a foot or numeral head. The second nearby curved stroke is the opening parenthesis. C prime/1 doubt resolved to prime.

Below and right of the final parenthesis a faint curved stroke with a darker tip survives, approximately at whole-source [1096,1560,1113,1572]. Its comma-like form is separate from the high black point. Comma is the preferred textual reading; a nontextual trace remains possible. It is not conflated with the high point.

notes: Coverage: I read the full assigned brief and packet, including the notation snapshot, then opened the whole page exactly once for layout, half_a exactly once, and half_b exactly once in that order. Every text block, every word and mark, and every inline mathematical expression was compared against both C and H. There are no display formulas, diagrams or drawings on this page. The twelve stored crops are one crop for each remaining locus or compact locus group; c12 checks an agreed word whose internal stroke remained open after the half view.

The complete page is handwritten. No generic handwritten wrappers are used. Its personal hand is not independently established from this packet, so the inventory uses an unnamed pen hand. No heading, date, author page number, salutation, signature or written page count is visible here. The lower-left 10 is preserved only as the archive sheet-number comment.

The opening noun is cancelled and replaced above by champs. The phrase s’obtient en is inserted before associant, and the interlinear L attaches after section. The hooks are ordinary insertion connectors and are represented by inserted at their attachment, not by detached figures. H’s editorial note acknowledges these same insertions, so macro spelling alone was not counted as a difference.

The page says that sigma is obtained from the symmetry of L tensor L, viewed as a section of ₂N. It then says Je sais prouver (sauf erreur) that every homomorphism M to ₂N comes from a suitable Picard champ. It places an a priori obstruction in Ext³(X;M,N) and asserts that a universal argument makes it zero. These are source assertions, not checks performed by this reader.

The next sentences call the extension alpha close to split, say every section on an object of X remonte, and paraphrase this as a set-theoretic section. They then claim the stronger provenance from the degree-two hypercohomology expression. The shortened live tte, the comma after alpha, and remonte are preserved without grammatical or mathematical normalization.

The two mathematical H signs are visibly cursive with loops. The retained caligraphic/script alternative concerns how best to render that pen alphabet using the supplied fonts; it is not evidence for a blackboard-bold H. The second occurrence uses the first candidate by the recurrence convention.

At the right edge after the final formula there are two physical marks, not one: a high black point and a lower pale curve with a darker tip. Both survive inside the edge. They are kept in their vertical relationship using overset, each with a textual/nontextual doubt; phantom alternatives denote uncertain textual status, not the absence of the physical marks.

Half-settled witness differences without a reader crop carry approximate whole-source boxes in their scan_shows fields. Their coordinate system is the 1130 by 1738 whole JPEG, origin at top left. The main reader should make and inspect adjudication crops at those boxes. The twelve existing crop paths supply direct evidence for the other loci.

No OCR, text-recognition software, PDF text layer, outside research, other scan image, other reader material, delegation, or LaTeX compilation was used. No mathematical proof or computation was performed; math_checks is therefore empty. The start timestamp is the first recorded UTC clock time after the brief was read.

C’s standalone cotefile prefix is omitted because the supplied convention permits it only on the first scan. H’s page 10 already represents the same archive number, so the required archive-number comment is not treated as a source omission in H. H’s remark about another dossier was not used as visual evidence.
